claim: The programme separates research, canonical semantics, implementation and publication authority.
primary_sources: Collaborative Intelligence AI_CONTEXT.md; Publication Pipeline README.md
counterargument_or_limit: Repository separation improves traceability but can increase coordination cost.

claim: The integrated system can be represented as a governed loop from reality through evidence and decision back to outcomes.
basis: Mission Framework architecture plus editorial synthesis
counterargument_or_limit: The integrated depiction has not been empirically validated as a whole.

claim: The Reality Belt adds explicit inbound challenge and outbound consequence tracking to the canonical Mission Loop.
counterargument_or_limit: The proposal may duplicate double-loop learning and theory-of-change practice.

claim: Human-AI combinations do not outperform the better of humans or AI by default.
counterargument_or_limit: Effects vary by task type and relative human/AI capability; study set largely predates frontier LLMs.

claim: AI assistance can improve immediate output while weakening later unaided performance.
counterargument_or_limit: One educational setting does not establish general deskilling.

claim: Stable collaboration depends on grounding and the distribution of repair work, not capability alone.
counterargument_or_limit: Sixteen interviews support theory-building, not prevalence or causal effect estimates.

claim: Human-AI collaboration design needs explicit activity, actor, authority, coordination and evaluation choices.
counterargument_or_limit: The 9A framework is conceptual and not yet empirically validated.

claim: Collective human-machine intelligence requires coordination of distributed cognitive resources and states.
basis: Peer-reviewed research agenda and sociocognitive architecture
counterargument_or_limit: The architecture is a research programme, not demonstrated system-level collective intelligence.

claim: Co-creation requires negotiated initiative, authorship and responsibility rather than mere AI participation.
counterargument_or_limit: The questionnaire included sixteen professionals and does not establish general effects.

claim: Human approval alone is an unreliable safeguard against automation bias.
counterargument_or_limit: Design, training and workload can change reliance; oversight is not uniformly ineffective.

claim: Evidence grades should distinguish empirical support, conceptual frameworks, programme propositions and normative commitments.
counterargument_or_limit: A compact grade can obscure study-level risk of bias unless the underlying register remains available.

claim: Demographic diversity does not guarantee better performance; information elaboration and authentic dissent are more plausible mechanisms.
primary_sources: van Dijk et al. 2012; Lu et al. 2012; Nemeth et al. 2001
counterargument_or_limit: Justice-based inclusion does not depend on a performance effect.

claim: The system should test benefits and restrictions together against strong baselines.
primary_sources: CI v2 RQ1-RQ8; Vaccaro et al. 2024
counterargument_or_limit: A single evaluation protocol may not transfer across domains or consequence levels.

claim: AI outputs remain analytical inputs; accountable humans or organisations retain consequential authority.
primary_sources: Mission Framework ARCHITECTURE.md; AI behavioural preamble
counterargument_or_limit: Human accountability can become a moral crumple zone if authority, time and competence are absent.

claim: Publication outputs must preserve authority boundaries, provenance and uncertainty.
primary_sources: Publication Pipeline README.md and Foundation 0.2 guidance
counterargument_or_limit: High provenance overhead can reduce usability unless adapted to audience and consequence.

claim: The next credible step is bounded comparative research, not a claim that the whole system works.
primary_sources: CI PR #14 review; Vaccaro et al. 2024
counterargument_or_limit: A narrow study will not validate the integrated architecture, only selected mechanisms.
